text: A Gromark key is a running number: each digit is the sum of two earlier digits, in some base. Each digit shifts one letter along the alphabet, so a base-b key can only shift by 0 to b-1.
Drawn for the sculpture's table: many known letters need a shift of 10 or more. On some table built from the puzzle's words the shifts might all be small.
Over 184,512 combinations of alphabets the smallest possible largest shift is 15. Bases 2 to 9 are dead before any rule is tried; base 10 and up were tested in experiments 46 and later.
